subject: USE statement
notes: kb/Work PB370 LANDED (w1091e): CONFORMS. Both refuter findings answered. (1) The identity claim now has a witness that can fail: conformance:cases/14.9.49-USE/pb370_exception_object_identity compares EXCEPTION-OBJECT with the object RAISEd AND with a second live instance of the same class (§8.8.4.2.15 'the same object'), for two successive raises (the register follows the raise) and inside a method's own declarative; oo_ec_raise_object (NOT = NULL only) is retired from this row. (2) The method half (DECLARATIVES in a method, COBOL0899) was closed by kb/Work PB1010; the golden's M1 leg enters a method's format 4 USE. || kb/Work PB370. Rule text (cite.py --check 14.9.49.4 "the predefined object reference EXCEPTION-OBJECT references the exception object" -> OK, GR 15). On BOTH paths that can enter a Format-4 declarative the register is set before the selector runs: EmitRaiseObject emits `ExceptionState.SetObject(<the RAISE operand>)` and then `__EcObjDispatch(ExceptionState.ExceptionObject)`; EmitPropagationPickup emits `SetObject(__po)` and then the selector. The covering case tests/conformance/2002/oo_ec_raise_object.cob enters the selected declarative and executes `SET U TO EXCEPTION-OBJECT` / `IF U NOT = NULL`, and the committed golden requires `BASE-HANDLER EXCEPTION-OBJECT` + `REGISTER-SET` - so the register is proven non-null and carrying the raised object on entry. Note the register is a run-unit-scoped single slot (ExceptionState.ExceptionObject) and a NAMED raise inside the declarative nulls it (Set sets ExceptionObject = null); that is 14.9.29.4 GR1's rule, and GR15 constrains only the state on ENTRY, which holds. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — Two independent defects in the record. (1) THE TEST-REF DOES NOT PIN THE RULE. GR15 says EXCEPTION-OBJECT 'references the exception object' -- an IDENTITY claim (ISO 8.8.4.2.15: the relation is true 'if the object referenced by identifier-3 is the same object that is referenced by identifier-4'). The cited conformance:cases/14.6.13.1.5-Exception-objects/oo_ec_raise_object asserts only 'IF U NOT = NULL DISPLAY "REGISTER-SET"'; its golden line 'REGISTER-SET' is satisfied by ANY non-null object, so a regression that set the register to the wrong object -- SELF, a fresh instance, the activating program -- keeps that golden green. The row is NOT closed by it and the test-ref must be emptied; the missing assertion is one line (IF U = E). I measured the identity claim myself and it HOLDS on every entry path, so the program-level half of the rule is genuinely correct -- this is a coverage correction, not a behaviour finding. (2) A HALF THAT CANNOT BE ENTERED AT ALL. 'the associated declarative' is a declarative in a procedure division, and ISO 14.2.2 SR10 permits the DECLARATIVES-bearing Format 1 (14.2.1) in a METHOD DEFINITION; StatementBinder.cs:239-242 rejects every declarative part inside a method with COBOL0899 'recognized but not yet implemented (owning roadmap phase: Phase 3, OO port)' at both 2002 and 2023, so a Format-4 USE in a method -- the natural home for EC-OO handling -- is legal source the compiler refuses. Unlocated/unreachable half + verified half => PARTIAL. (Contributing, already owned by the record for GR14: the interface-name-1 arm of the associated declarative is rejected COBOL0859, so even in a program only the object-class arm of GR14 can ever deliver an entry for GR15 to constrain -- I confirmed that rejection. It does not by itself move GR15, because the register is written BEFORE the selector runs and is therefore arm-independent.) || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 2002/2014/2023 (FORMAT 4). No Annex E entry touches it. retired-witness: conformance:cases/14.6.13.1.5-Exception-objects/oo_ec_raise_object (asserts only EXCEPTION-OBJECT NOT = NULL, which any non-null object satisfies; GR15 is an identity claim (refuter, kb/Work PB370))
